events.title: Scala 3.0 released
events.summary: The Scala team released Scala 3.0 on May 4, 2021 — a major redesign with optional braces, union types, and a new compiler (Dotty).
events.about: Scala 3 simplified syntax (`if x then y`), added powerful type-level features, and improved [Java] interop. It aimed to keep Scala relevant for data engineering (Spark) and typed [functional programming] without the boilerplate critics blamed on Scala 2.

narrative.whyChosen: Scala 3 was a once-per-decade language revision for a major [JVM] language.
narrative.whyImportant: It reset Scala's design after years of complexity complaints from teams.
narrative.problemSolved: Scala 2's syntax and implicit-heavy style scared away teams who wanted [JVM] types without ceremony.

events.title: Erlang/OTP 24 released
events.summary: The [Erlang]/[OTP] team released [OTP] 24 on May 12, 2021 with [JIT] compilation, improved SSL/[TLS], and enhanced observer tools.
events.about: [OTP] 24's [JIT] sped hot [Erlang] and [Elixir] code paths without changing semantics — a boost for Phoenix and RabbitMQ workloads. Updated crypto and socket APIs kept [BEAM] applications current for telecom, messaging, and fintech backends.

narrative.whyChosen: [OTP] 24's [JIT] was the biggest [BEAM] performance leap in years.
narrative.whyImportant: Faster [Erlang] benefited the entire [Elixir] ecosystem built on the same VM.
narrative.problemSolved: [BEAM] [bytecode] interpretation lagged behind [JIT]-equipped runtimes for [CPU]-heavy tasks.

events.title: Bootstrap 5 released
events.summary: Bootstrap 5.0 shipped on May 5, 2021 — dropping jQuery, adding RTL support, and refreshing components for the utility-first era.
events.about: Bootstrap 5 removed jQuery entirely, added offcanvas and updated forms, and improved dark-mode hooks — staying relevant as [Tailwind] grew. It remains the fastest path to a polished admin [UI] without designing from scratch.

narrative.whyChosen: Bootstrap 5 kept the framework current by shedding jQuery and adding modern layout features.
narrative.whyImportant: Vanilla JS and RTL support aligned Bootstrap with contemporary front-end practices.
narrative.problemSolved: jQuery dependency and legacy components made Bootstrap feel dated next to newer toolkits.

events.title: Squarespace direct listing
events.summary: Squarespace began trading on the NYSE on May 19, 2021 under ticker SQSP — a direct listing at a $50 reference price valuing the company at roughly $6.5 billion.
events.about: Unlike a traditional [IPO], Squarespace's direct listing let existing shareholders sell without issuing new shares — following Spotify and [Slack]'s playbook. The debut validated website builders as a mature public [SaaS] category.

narrative.whyChosen: Squarespace's NYSE debut marked website builders as public-market businesses.
narrative.whyImportant: Direct listings offered an alternative path to public markets for [SaaS] companies.
narrative.problemSolved: Mature [SaaS] companies wanted public liquidity without dilutive [IPO] share issuance.

events.title: Colonial Pipeline shut down by ransomware
events.summary: Colonial Pipeline halted fuel deliveries on May 7, 2021 after a DarkSide [ransomware] attack — causing gas shortages across the U.S. East Coast and a $4.4 million [Bitcoin] ransom payment.
events.about: A single compromised [VPN] password without MFA took down critical energy infrastructure. The Biden administration responded with executive orders on cybersecurity; insurers raised [ransomware] premiums; and developers in OT-adjacent [SaaS] faced new customer security questionnaires about MFA, segmentation, and backup isolation.

narrative.whyChosen: Colonial Pipeline proved [ransomware] could affect physical-world fuel supplies, not just data.
narrative.whyImportant: It triggered U.S. government action and corporate MFA mandates at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing until recovery — legacy OT networks met modern criminal [ransomware] economics.
